title: A Superdiffusive Local Limit Theorem for the Elephant Random Walk and the Breakdown of Log-Concavity
summary: Let $(S_n)_{n\geq 1}$ be the one-dimensional Elephant Random Walk (ERW) in the superdiffusive regime, with memory parameter $p\in(3/4,1)$ and first-step bias $\mathbb{P}(S_1=1)=q$. Set $a=2p-1\in(1/2,1)$. If $f_{q,a}$ denotes the density of the superdiffusive limit $L_{q,a}$, we prove the uniform local limit theorem $\lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{j\in\mathbb{Z},\,j\equiv n\;(\mathrm{mod}\;2)}\left|\frac{n^a}{2}\mathbb{P}(S_n=j)-f_{q,a}(j/n^a)\right|=0$. The proof uses the exact recurrence for the probability mass function of $S_n$, yielding uniform $O(n^{-a})$ and $O(n^{-2a})$ bounds for the p.m.f.…
